topics: Latency vs cost tradeoffs and batching
transcript:
[00:00] Sofia (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call? We have Marcus, Priya, Aisha from Orion, and Ethan from Redwood.
[00:12] Marcus: Yep, Marcus here. Morning.
[00:15] Priya: Priya on the line.
[00:17] Aisha: Aisha here.
[00:20] Ethan (SE): Ethan here. Good to see you all.
[00:24] Sofia: Cool, agenda is model selection updates, pinning strategy, rollback/fallback, and action items. We'll try to keep to 45.
[00:28] Marcus: Sounds good.
[01:05] Priya: Quick update from our side: we ran the set of inference passes on rdx-2 baseline and rdx-3 as you suggested, rough numbers show rdx-3 is slightly more accurate on our NER and product categorization tests but costs ~2.2x tokens/latency.
[01:35] Ethan: Right, that matches our lab numbers somewhat, rdx-3 gets better semantic recall but at higher per-token time. Did you run with quantization?
[01:45] Priya: We did a q8 bench on rdx-2, and q4-ish on rdx-3 but the rdx-3 quant seems touchy; we've got some hallucination cases creeping in when aggressive quantization applied.
[02:10] Sofia: Okay so main tradeoff is accuracy vs cost/latency. For the POC goal — 95% catalog match and sub-600ms p95 — which way does it point?
[02:25] Priya: Right now rdx-2-quant hits the latency target in staging at p95 ~540ms with batching set to 8, accuracy is at ~93.5% on the sample set. rdx-3 is at 96% but p95 is 1.2s on the same infra.
[02:48] Marcus: Cost is also a concern; at scale the 1.2s p95 is going to double our token bill.
[03:05] Ethan: Two practical options: pin route to rdx-2-quant for now and run targeted rdx-3 for high-risk flows (e.g., high-value transactions), or use a rollout with weights and automatic fallback if latency SLOs are missed.
[03:30] Aisha: From security side, we also want the ability to pin to a private deployment later. Does pinning support Dedicated or VPC variants?
[03:42] Ethan: Yep, pinning is per-route and per-deployment. You can pin route A to hosted rdx-2-quant and route B to your Dedicated pool later. The control plane supports route-level version pins and can reference deployment tags.
[04:05] Sofia: Note I'll send the doc that outlines how to pin by route and how rollbacks work — it has the step-by-step and examples.
[04:18] Priya: Great. One question — if we pin to rdx-2-v1 and later want to roll to rdx-2-v2, can we do canary percentages with automatic fallback?
[04:30] Ethan: Yes. You can do percentage-based rollouts (e.g., 5% -> 25% -> 100%) and define failure conditions (latency, error rate, quality regression). If any trigger hits the platform auto-rolls back to the previous pinned version or fallback model like rdx-1.
[04:55] Marcus: How deterministic are the regression checks? We need reproducible metrics for our SREs.
[05:05] Ethan: We emit token-level latency, request traces, and per-prompt similarity scores if you upload ground truth. The rollback triggers can be configured with absolute thresholds and a lookback window so behavior is deterministic.
[05:25] Marcus: Okay good.
[06:00] Priya: On the sample dataset: we noticed some NER edge cases where brand names formatted weirdly — do you want us to add those to the eval set?
[06:12] Sofia: Yes please. The more representative the eval the better. We'll use them in the quality monitors.
[06:20] Priya: I'll attach a 10k sample subset and labels to the shared folder by Thursday.
[06:30] Aisha: Security question — KMS integration for Dedicated. We have an internal KMS (HashiVault) and need to know if Redwood supports custom KMS/HSM and the onboarding process.
[06:42] Ethan: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations. For Hatchi— sorry HashiVault — we've onboarded similar setups; we'll need a short security call and the KMS endpoint details. We can also provide SOC2 docs; Sofia will share contacts.
[07:10] Sofia: I'll share the SOC2 and the security questionnaire after the call.
[07:17] Marcus: Awesome.
[07:50] Priya: Back to model decisions — what about fallback to hosted smaller models instead of dedicated? For example fallback to rdx-1 hosted when rdx-2-quant p95 exceeds threshold.
[08:05] Ethan: That's valid. You can set fallback to a cheaper hosted model. The platform supports cross-deployment fallbacks — e.g., if Dedicated pool is throttled, route to hosted rdx-1. There is a small cold-start risk but it's generally fine for our use-case.
[08:28] Marcus: Cold start risk is okay for low-frequency flows. For checkout suggestions we need low jitter.
[08:41] Sofia: Suggestion: pin the critical checkout route to rdx-2-quant and set a stricter SLO plus a canary with rdx-3 for complex catalog mapping. Non-critical routes can default to rdx-1.
[09:05] Priya: Doable. We'll prioritize checkout and product-normalization routes.
[09:15] Ethan: On the benchmark front, I'll run a 1k-request flattened benchmark on staging with rdx-2-quant pinned and batching 8/12 to measure p95 and tokens/sec. I'll include KV cache warm runs and cold runs.
[09:35] Marcus: Please include both 4k and 8k context lengths — product descriptions vary.
[09:44] Ethan: Will do.
[10:12] Aisha: Another compliance note: retention — we need the ability to opt-out of retaining prompt payloads in the hosted logs. Can Redwood do per-client retention policies?
[10:24] Ethan: Yes, we have per-tenant retention controls and you can disable prompt persistence on hosted. For Dedicated the logs can be configured to stay in your VPC.
[10:38] Marcus: Good.
[11:05] Priya: Quick nit — in your docs rdx-2 is sometimes referenced as redwood-rdx2 or rdx2; just want consistent naming for the perf csv.
[11:16] Sofia: Noted, we'll standardize to "rdx-2-quant" and include alias column.
[11:30] Priya: Thanks.
[12:05] Marcus: Any concerns about throughput? If we pin many routes to rdx-2 we might saturate the pool. How does Dedicated autoscaling behave?
[12:20] Ethan: Dedicated autoscale can be configured with target throughput, burst capacity, and pre-warmed nodes. For POC we recommend a small dedicated pool or use hosted with guaranteed qps during peak windows. We'll provide autoscale config examples.
[12:42] Sofia: I'll share the autoscale examples and cost tradeoffs doc.
[12:50] Marcus: Great.
[13:20] Aisha: On the KMS onboarding — is there an expected lead time? 
[13:28] Ethan: Typically 2-3 weeks to validate and exchange certs for an HSM-backed setup, less for standard KMS cloud integrations.
[13:36] Aisha: Ok, sounds fine.
[14:05] Priya: Can we run a rollback test intentionally? Like simulate a latency spike and confirm the auto-fallback?
[14:14] Ethan: Absolutely — you can create a fault-injection test or we can simulate load and set the threshold low for the canary. I suggest doing this on staging next week.
[14:30] Marcus: Let's plan that.
[15:00] Sofia: Quick recap — agreed: pin checkout route to rdx-2-quant, run 1k benchmark with context variants, share pricing + perf CSV, prepare a canary rollback test on staging w/c 2027-06-28.
[15:18] Priya: We'll provide the 10k sample set and labels by Thursday.
[15:25] Aisha: We'll confirm KMS requirements and SOC2 contact by Friday.
[15:40] Sofia: Perfect. Anything else?
[15:45] Marcus: One minor ask — can you include a cost projection at 10M monthly queries using both rdx-2 pinned and rdx-3 selective?
[15:55] Sofia: Yes, I'll include in the pricing sheet.
[16:10] Ethan: Also, I'll attach the benchmark script and the exact request payload shape so you can reproduce.
[16:20] Priya: Great.
[16:45] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[44:10] Sofia: Alright thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links and the action items. Meeting adjourned.
[44:30] Ethan: Thanks, bye.
[44:35] Priya: Bye.
[44:40] Aisha: Thanks, bye.
